Review Title: Not too bad for the price
Review: UPDATE.... It has been about a month since I purchased these bags and they are working well.  The one thing is that I would definitely due is put a spring loaded paper clip to hold the velcro flap closed. By the end of the first day the velcro does not feel very secure and I feel that it could open if the bag was very full. I do wrap up a small piece of paper towel over the flap before I install the spring loaded paper clip. This prevents the sharp edges of the paper clip from cutting into velcro flap. Otherwise the bags work out to be $1.80 per bag versus $5.20 for a similar Convatec bag. A very big saving. I still use the Hollister 7805 barrier ring with this bag and I have no leaks. What a savings with this bag.I have used Convatec and Hollister bags for years, I thought I would give these a try. First they are half the cost of other bags. The flange is thinner which actually makes it more flexible which is a good thing. It bends  easier then you sit or bend over. Again this is a good thing. I have always used the Hollister 7805 barrier ring to make sure I have a good seal. I am using the 7805 barrier ring with these bags and I am not experiencing any leaks.When I first got my ostomy, the ostomy nurse told me that using a barrier ring with the bag was necessary. She told me using any ostomy bag without a barrier ring would always cause a problem with leakage. So far so good with these cheaper ostomy bags.The one think some people complained about was the velcro closer at the bottom of the bag. The first day the velcro closure did feel secure. By the end of the day the velcro was feeling a little weak so I did put a clip on the velcro to make it more secure.  This is the one problem area of the bag. Putting a clip on the velcro strip did solve the problem and for the price of the bag I did not complain.I will update this review as i use these ostomy bags over the next few weeks. So far for the price, it is a good deal.I just want to add that the bags are semi transparent.

Review: I feel the one star reviews for this product are REALLY unfair. There are a lot of things not quite right about these bags but they work ok and the price can't be beat. There is no filter even though it looks like there is one at the top.  The advice is to push a pin whole through the top which is plain silly since it lets the smell out. To solve this problem I've been using the smallest clip from an office supply store which sounds goofy but works find.  The seal is good and not that hard to remove.  I've never had a "blow out" or had the bag break.  I'm especially impressed since I have a peristomal hernia that goes out about 3 inches and it still manages to seal quite well.  I know it sounds like a lot but I've gotten used to it and, once again, it's GREAT for the price; change it a day earlier than the more expensive bags and you'll always have a clean one with not problem.

Review Title: Great for descending area colostomy, as good as Hollister 8331, half the price
Review: I purchased these because of the closure style (folding velcro that is EXCELLENT) and the single piece with a more flexible wafer, being a new user of a stoma bag due to cancer while having chemo before reattachment surgery.  I can say that these are much better for me than the two-piece Hollisters because the colloidal portion does flex better than the 2-piece's wafer due to my stoma being just below my ribcage. It adheres well and I usually get 3-4 days out of them. Mine tend to leak at the end of their life at the side by my centerline/navel, but that's due to my abdomen and how I sit, and the pressure I put on it, not the product. The white outer tape actually serves as a way to quickly glance and see if you're leaking as well.Like any bag, if you are sweating in the heat or showering, this outer tape will come loose quickly if it gets too wet, however, so be careful. When it does get the outer tape loose, the colloidal still adheres well. I use Goo-Gone medical grade 8oz bottle of remover with this, it takes it right off cleanly to let you gently peel the colloidal, it seems to fare well with body hair as well.  It can leave a small residue/ring that you may need to clean up.The end with the velcro closure DOES take a moment to figure out, you pinch from the outsides inward to get it to open, but emptying it isn't really a problem. I can hold it open with one hand after using two to pinch it open, so I can clean the opening before re-closing it. The bag is pretty durable, I have yet to puncture one, and I even have rolled onto it in my sleep without any problem (knock on wood). When closed, it is just short of being able to be tucked in my waistband, and it doesn't tug on me with weight. Lubrication drops inside with this makes it a dream to deal with, however.I would say the closest thing to this is the Hollister 8331 bag, and it's half the price of it.  Not having to deal with my insurance and still pay the same amount is good enough for me.  I may be a newbie at this, but I've already tried many bags in the 7 weeks since my surgery, and I can say these are great for me. The price isn't a bad thing either. Your mileage may vary, but these are my mainstay now.

Review Title: Easy to use kit. Comes with most everything you need.
Review: Having to deal with a Ostomy medical procedure and then having to deal with a suppressed diet makes and then having to get the right colostomy supplies and making sure they work for you is stressful and disheartening. If you can make it simpler, that would be one less thing to have to worry about. The Heagimed Ostomy supplies tkaes this into consideration when they put this kit together. The 22 piece kit comes with 16 Ostomy bags and 6 round skin barriers. The bags are comfortable to wear and have a soft texture outside. There is a carbon filter built in to filter out odors. The best thing about this bag is that it has a hook and loop closure for ease of use. Instead of using a clamp to seal the bag, you simply peel open and close the bag end like any Velcro bag.  The skin barrier ring seems to do it's job of preventing waste from coming out and keeps the bag secure. You do have to tailor the size and fit of the opening to the size of the stoma. The kit comes with instructional guides which makes it easy to use. I'm glad that I could find such a simple kit that has everything I need. Now I don't have to buy the bag and the skin barrier separately and wonder if they will work well together.

Description: Colostomy Bags, Ostomy Supplies,One Piece Drainable Ostomy Pouch
Review Title: You get what you pay for
Review: I tried these bags while I was in between insurances, and didn't want to pay out of pocket for my regular brand. These bags are inexpensive, and I am sure that they work great for some folks. Unfortunately, I am not one of those that it worked great for.I usually change my Hollister setup once every 7-9 days. These bags I changed three times in one week.My skin was not very happy. It wasn't happy with the bag adhesive and it wasn't happy with the frequent changes. I must say though, that my skin is not happy with most products, and is definitely not happy with frequent changes.The reason for the frequent changes was that the bag didn't hold up. I use a wafer and paste underneath and for some reason they just dissolved under this bag. Two bags blew out the side and the third the Velcro gave out (although that wasn't the worst problem. I was able to use a bobby pin to hold it together). When I went to change that bag, it was obvious that it was also about to go.I started questioning myself, wondering what I was doing wrong. I have had my stoma for three years now, and have had very few mishaps since.I put on when it my emergency Hollisters, and I haven't had any issues (other than my skin itching from healing). So now I'm just waiting for my shipment from edgepark.If you are used to frequent bag changes, this may be the right choice for you. Every body is different, and mine is just super picky. It's a bummer though since these are so much cheaper and the bags themselves are soft and thick (although the way it empties caught me off guard the first time, so beware of that).

Product Name: 20 PCS Colostomy Bags, Ostomy Supplies,One Piece Drainable Ostomy Pouch with Hook and Loop Closure for Ileostomy Stoma Care, 15mm-60mm Cut to Fit
Description: Colostomy Bags, Ostomy Supplies,One Piece Drainable Ostomy Pouch
Review: I don't know if this product was too old when they sent it to me, or if it was just poorly made, but it has been a frustrating experience. First, the adhesive that is supposed to hold a seal around the stoma area only stays stuck for a few hours before it loses stickiness. Yes, a few hours. Sometimes you can get them to stick for a day, but that is very rare, so you end up with a lot of bad smells, lots more bags used than one would like, and a chant going through your mind of "please don't get diarrhea now, please don't get diarrhea now." Then there's the opening at the bottom, which is supposed to be a velcro seal ... that doesn't stay sealed for even 60 seconds. There are little round white stickers that come in the box, and yep, they don't work for sealing it closed, either. I am now running around with a bag clip (like you'd clip closed a bag of chips) clipped to the bottom of my colostomy bag to keep it closed.

Product Name: 20 PCS Colostomy Bags, Ostomy Supplies,One Piece Drainable Ostomy Pouch with Hook and Loop Closure for Ileostomy Stoma Care, 15mm-60mm Cut to Fit
Description: Colostomy Bags, Ostomy Supplies,One Piece Drainable Ostomy Pouch
Review Title: Using binder clip at the opening fixes the problem of accidental opening!
Review: A great value, once I solved the problem with the spout. It's unforgivable that the bag opens accidentally at the spout, but a small binder clip makes this bag at least as secure as Hollister, for a fraction of the cost! I use the 3/4" small binder clips  https://www.amazon.com/Officemate-Binder-Clips-Small-99220/dp/B0C9R5SJSF?th=1, and always carry a few spares with my supplies. I haven't had an accidental opening since. The adhesion of the ring is decent (I noticed some reviewers said too hard to remove while others said not sticky enough). I once developed a rash, which cleared up by first applying a layer of Tegaderm (which uses a less irrating adhesive, but it didn't stick as well).

Review Title: Not too bad for the price
Review: UPDATE.... It has been about a month since I purchased these bags and they are working well.  The one thing is that I would definitely due is put a spring loaded paper clip to hold the velcro flap closed. By the end of the first day the velcro does not feel very secure and I feel that it could open if the bag was very full. I do wrap up a small piece of paper towel over the flap before I install the spring loaded paper clip. This prevents the sharp edges of the paper clip from cutting into velcro flap. Otherwise the bags work out to be $1.80 per bag versus $5.20 for a similar Convatec bag. A very big saving. I still use the Hollister 7805 barrier ring with this bag and I have no leaks. What a savings with this bag.I have used Convatec and Hollister bags for years, I thought I would give these a try. First they are half the cost of other bags. The flange is thinner which actually makes it more flexible which is a good thing. It bends  easier then you sit or bend over. Again this is a good thing. I have always used the Hollister 7805 barrier ring to make sure I have a good seal. I am using the 7805 barrier ring with these bags and I am not experiencing any leaks.When I first got my ostomy, the ostomy nurse told me that using a barrier ring with the bag was necessary. She told me using any ostomy bag without a barrier ring would always cause a problem with leakage. So far so good with these cheaper ostomy bags.The one think some people complained about was the velcro closer at the bottom of the bag. The first day the velcro closure did feel secure. By the end of the day the velcro was feeling a little weak so I did put a clip on the velcro to make it more secure.  This is the one problem area of the bag. Putting a clip on the velcro strip did solve the problem and for the price of the bag I did not complain.I will update this review as i use these ostomy bags over the next few weeks. So far for the price, it is a good deal.I just want to add that the bags are semi transparent.

Review Title: Not perfect but GREAT for the price
Review: I feel the one star reviews for this product are REALLY unfair. There are a lot of things not quite right about these bags but they work ok and the price can't be beat.  I was using the Coloplast Sensura Mia and still have them. But for lock down these are better.  They sometimes sound like you have an empty bag of cheetos in your pocket. There is no filter even though it looks like there is one at the top.  The advice is to push a pin whole through the top which is plain silly since it lets the smell out.  I'm going to experiment with an external filter and let you know how it goes.  As a result they have to be continually "burped", The cover is not completely opaque.  And yet, they seal without an extra ring (the Mia doesn't for me) and cost about two bucks a bag.  )lately I've been using a sealing ring). There is no easy way to fold the neck up into the bag cover to keep liquid from draining to the bottom and making it hard to reseal the velcro.  To solve this problem I've been using the smallest clip from an office supply store which sounds goofy but works find.  The seal is good and not that hard to remove.  I've never had a "blow out" or had the bag break.  I'm especially impressed since I have a peristomal hernia that goes out about 3 inches and it still manages to seal quite well.  I know it sounds like a lot but I've gotten used to it and, once again, it's GREAT for the price; change it a day earlier than the more expensive bags and you'll always have a clean one with not problem.

Review Title: Great for descending area colostomy, as good as Hollister 8331, half the price
Review: I purchased these because of the closure style (folding velcro that is EXCELLENT) and the single piece with a more flexible wafer, being a new user of a stoma bag due to cancer while having chemo before reattachment surgery.  I can say that these are much better for me than the two-piece Hollisters because the colloidal portion does flex better than the 2-piece's wafer due to my stoma being just below my ribcage. It adheres well and I usually get 3-4 days out of them. Mine tend to leak at the end of their life at the side by my centerline/navel, but that's due to my abdomen and how I sit, and the pressure I put on it, not the product. The white outer tape actually serves as a way to quickly glance and see if you're leaking as well.Like any bag, if you are sweating in the heat or showering, this outer tape will come loose quickly if it gets too wet, however, so be careful. When it does get the outer tape loose, the colloidal still adheres well. I use Goo-Gone medical grade 8oz bottle of remover with this, it takes it right off cleanly to let you gently peel the colloidal, it seems to fare well with body hair as well.  It can leave a small residue/ring that you may need to clean up.The end with the velcro closure DOES take a moment to figure out, you pinch from the outsides inward to get it to open, but emptying it isn't really a problem. I can hold it open with one hand after using two to pinch it open, so I can clean the opening before re-closing it. The bag is pretty durable, I have yet to puncture one, and I even have rolled onto it in my sleep without any problem (knock on wood). When closed, it is just short of being able to be tucked in my waistband, and it doesn't tug on me with weight. Lubrication drops inside with this makes it a dream to deal with, however.I would say the closest thing to this is the Hollister 8331 bag, and it's half the price of it.  Not having to deal with my insurance and still pay the same amount is good enough for me.  I may be a newbie at this, but I've already tried many bags in the 7 weeks since my surgery, and I can say these are great for me. The price isn't a bad thing either. Your mileage may vary, but these are my mainstay now.
